quizSubtitle: Find the right device for your child
reassurance: Whatever you choose, you're already doing the right thing by thinking about this. There's no perfect answer — just the right one for your family.

questions.text: What's the main reason your child needs a device?
questions.subtitle: Select all that apply

questions.text: Does your child need a camera on their device?

pros: Lets your child capture memories and express creativity
Useful for homework, scanning QR codes, and practical everyday tasks
cons: Can contribute to selfie culture and appearance-based comparison
Many smartphone-free schools don't allow camera phones on site
Opens the door to inappropriate photo sharing

options.label: Nice to have but not essential

questions.text: What kind of messaging does your child need?

pros: Access to the group chats that friends and family already use
Free messaging, calls, and media sharing worldwide
Standard texting now supports group messages and photo sharing — so your child can do more than you'd think without needing WhatsApp
cons: Group chats can expose your child to content you can't control
Creates pressure to be 'always on' and respond immediately
Harder to monitor than simple calls and texts

questions.text: Is it important to you to be able to see where your child is?

pros: Real-time location tracking gives genuine peace of mind
Particularly valuable when children first start travelling independently
Some trackers include SOS buttons for emergencies
cons: Can feel like surveillance and undermine trust-building
GPS drains battery — devices need charging more often

options.label: No, I trust them to check in

questions.text: Should the device have any internet access?

pros: Access to maps, music streaming, and educational content
Prepares your child for the digital world with guardrails in place
Needed for some school apps and homework resources
cons: Opens the door to unfiltered content, social media, and endless rabbit holes
'Limited' access can be hard to enforce — children find workarounds
The closer the device is to a smartphone, the harder it is to draw the line

questions.text: What kind of screen feels right?

pros: Feels 'normal' to children — reduces social pressure and resistance
Easier and more intuitive to use
More accessible for children with additional needs
cons: The closer it looks to a smartphone, the closer it feels to one
More expensive and more fragile than basic-screen devices
More tempting to pick up and use excessively

questions.text: Does your child's school have a phone policy?
How much do you care about your child having a device that looks like a smartphone?

topicDetail.prosTitle: Pros of looking like a smartphone
topicDetail.consTitle: Cons of looking like a smartphone
pros: Reduces social friction — friends are less likely to comment or tease
Your child is more likely to actually want to carry and use it
Feels 'normal' in social settings like school pick-up or clubs
cons: A smartphone-looking device can create smartphone-level expectations
More expensive — touchscreen devices cost more than basic phones
Harder to explain why it can't do what a real smartphone does

options.label: A lot — it'll make things easier for them
Somewhat — a modern look would help but it's not essential
Not at all — I'd prefer it didn't look like a smartphone

questions.subtitle: Select all price ranges you'd consider

devices.name: Nokia 105 2G
devices.summary: Ultra-basic calls and texts with an incredible battery that lasts for weeks. No camera, no internet, no distractions.
devices.bestFor: Families who want the simplest possible phone — just calls and texts, nothing else — at a price where it doesn't matter if it gets lost.

devices.name: TCL 4022S
devices.summary: A budget-friendly basic phone with an SOS button for emergencies. Has a very basic camera but no internet or apps.
devices.bestFor: Families on a tight budget who want a simple phone with the added safety of an emergency SOS button.

devices.name: Karri
devices.summary: A screenless voice messenger with GPS tracking. Children send and receive voice messages and calls — nothing else.
devices.bestFor: Younger children who need to stay in touch and be trackable, without any screen time at all.

devices.name: GPO 746
devices.summary: A VoIP home landline that plugs into your broadband. Your child can call and answer calls at home — no mobile needed.
devices.bestFor: Families who want their child reachable at home without giving them a mobile device at all.

devices.name: Nokia 2660 Flip
devices.summary: A stylish 4G flip phone with calls, texts and a basic camera. Has a browser, but pair with a data-free SIM to keep it simple.
devices.bestFor: Children who want something that looks cool and feels grown-up, without the risks of a smartphone. Pair with a data-free SIM to block internet access.

devices.name: The Phone+
devices.summary: A touchscreen phone that only does calls and texts — no camera, no internet, no GPS. Looks like a smartphone but isn't one.
devices.bestFor: Children who care about having a 'normal-looking' phone but whose parents want zero internet access. Reduces social pressure while keeping things simple.

devices.name: XploraOne
devices.summary: A touchscreen 'startphone' with calls, texts, GPS tracking and a camera — but no internet, apps or social media.
devices.bestFor: Families who want their child contactable and trackable, with a modern-looking device that's safe for school.

devices.name: HMD Fusion X1
devices.summary: A child-safe smartphone with 5G, managed apps, GPS tracking and full parental controls. Looks and feels like a real phone — with guardrails.
devices.bestFor: Older children ready for more independence, where parents want to gradually introduce features with full oversight. A genuine stepping stone to a full smartphone.

devices.name: Pinwheel
devices.summary: A customised Android phone with 1,000+ vetted apps, GPS tracking and detailed parental controls. Parents choose exactly which apps to enable.
devices.bestFor: Families who want smartphone-level flexibility but with full control over what's available. Great for children who need specific apps for school or hobbies.

devices.name: Balance Phone
devices.summary: A restricted Android phone with WhatsApp, Spotify and Maps built in — but no social media, no browser, no app store.
devices.bestFor: Teens who need WhatsApp to stay in group chats and Maps for getting around, but whose parents want to keep social media and open browsing off the table.

devices.name: Light Phone II
devices.summary: A beautifully minimalist e-ink phone for calls, texts, music and podcasts. No browser, no social media, no distractions. Designed for people who want less.
devices.bestFor: Older teens (or parents!) who actively want a calmer relationship with technology. A statement piece that says 'I choose to disconnect.'
